fixes.explanation: Riches and family never come up in this verse. The psalmist is talking to the One whose hands made him, and what he asks for is “…understanding to learn Your commandments.” That's the whole request. I think that's a mighty good thing to ask your Maker for.
Word is it. He says, “…for I have hoped in Your word.” His hope is in what God has said. That's a sturdy place to put your weight.
I know the word law can sound heavy. But the psalmist says, “…for Your law is my delight.” Delight, not burden. I think that's a joyful way to look at it, friend.
Secret doesn't show up here. The psalmist says, “…for Your law is my delight.” Delight is the word he uses, and nothing in the verse says anything about keeping it hidden.

That's a sad question, but the psalmist doesn't ask it here. He asks, “When will You comfort me?” He's waiting, and what he wants is comfort. The question is about comfort and timing, not about why he was made.

Close, but it's the other way around. The psalmist says, “Though I am like a wineskin dried up by smoke, I do not forget Your statutes.” He compares himself to a dried-up wineskin, and he still doesn't forget them. That little word “Though” is carrying a lot.

False. He says, “Though I am like a wineskin dried up by smoke, I do not forget Your statutes.” He compares himself to a wineskin dried up by smoke, and he still says he does not forget. I bet that comparison means he's feeling worn out, but the verse itself only gives us the picture.

Yes. He says, “I am persecuted without cause—help me!” Without cause means the persecution isn't justified. And he says it right after calling all of God's commandments faithful. I think that's a heavy thing to carry.

The text says the opposite. The psalmist says, “They almost wiped me from the earth, but I have not forsaken Your precepts.” The ones who almost wiped him out are the persecutors. What he hasn't forsaken is God's precepts, so the answer is True.

Silence doesn't appear in this verse. The psalmist asks, “Revive me according to Your loving devotion, that I may obey the testimony of Your mouth.” What he asks for is revival and obeying. Silence has no place in either blank.
That's the big one. He says, “Your word, O LORD, is everlasting; it is firmly fixed in the heavens.” Everlasting and firmly fixed. That's a lot of staying power in one verse.

The psalmist doesn't say anything about hidden. He says, “Your word, O LORD, is everlasting; it is firmly fixed in the heavens.” Everlasting and firmly fixed is what he says about it. Nothing in this verse says it's hard to find.
Almost, but the second half is the problem. The psalmist says, “You established the earth, and it endures.” Endures, not fades. God established the earth, and it endures.

Enemies come up plenty in this psalm, but not in this verse. The psalmist says, “Your ordinances stand to this day, for all things are servants to You.” The word he uses for all things is servants. That's the word that fills the blank.

Treasures is a nice guess, friend, but I'd keep that word for the cookie jar. The psalmist says, “Your ordinances stand to this day, for all things are servants to You.” ALL things, servants to Him. That's the word he picked.

That's what he says. “If Your law had not been my delight, then I would have perished in my affliction.” He's looking back at the hard stretch and naming what he says kept him from perishing. I think that's a heavy thing to say.

Bless is a lovely word, but it's not in this verse. The psalmist says, “I am Yours; save me, for I have sought Your precepts.” What he asks for is saving. The reason he gives is that he has sought God's precepts.

It's the other way around, friend. The psalmist says, “I have seen a limit to all perfection, but Your commandment is without limit.” He has seen a limit to all perfection, and he says God's commandment is without limit. That little word “but” is doing the work.
False, you've got it. He says, “I have seen a limit to all perfection, but Your commandment is without limit.” He has seen a limit to all perfection. God's commandment is without limit.
